newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures end firm, crosses boost volume.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures end firm, crosses boost volume.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa ended firmer across the board on Thursday, with help from New York's gap higher at the open.
Benchmark May cocoa ended up 17 stg at 1,032 stg per tonne, one tick off its session high. Thursday's high of 1,033 stg matched Wednesday's high and could be seen as a double top on daily charts.
New York's gains encouraged some short-covering and new longs into the market after two days of sharp losses there.

However, London traders were not yet convinced cocoa would resume its upward path. They said outright activity was still thin and volatile, marked by local trade, which can exaggerate price movements in either direction.

Crosses dominated London's activity, grabbing the bulk of Thursday's volume of 9,698 contracts. Mees Pierson's 2,050 distant May/December cross in the morning between 41 and 43 stg was seen as the day's highlight.

The market was expected to consolidate nervously at higher levels, with first resistance at 1,035 and then, around 1,048-50, traders and analysts said. Support was pegged at 989 and 982, the bottom of a gap.
Traders expect the market to consolidate further while charts are correcting from oversold levels.
But forecasts for dry weather in Ghana and the Ivory Coast over the next few days were seen limiting any losses.
Light rains in southern Ivory Coast's cocoa belt eased off in the last weeks after breaking a drought that had threatened to reduce the midcrop, crop analysts in Abidjan said.
